content.text:
I could not run `npm test` or any node scripts, because the Bash tool was denied in this session. Everything below comes from reading `src/todo.js`, `bin/todo.js` and the tests, so the repros are traced by hand and unexecuted. I edited nothing.

## Confirmed bugs

1. **Tags are lost when a recurring todo is rescheduled.** `src/todo.js:138-140`
   - `completeAndReschedule` creates `next` with only title, due, priority, `repeat` and `repeatDay`. It never copies `item.tags`.
   - Repro: `addRecurring("rent","monthly",{due:"2026-01-31"})`, `addTag(1,"home")`, then `completeAndReschedule(1)`. The new item has no tags, so `list --tag home` and `search home` stop finding the live occurrence.
   - Fix: after creating `next`, add `if (item.tags?.length) next.tags = [...item.tags];`.

2. **`recur` is accepted on a done item, and it silently does nothing.** `bin/todo.js:226-235`
   - The CLI checks for a missing item and a missing due date, but not `item.done`.
   - Once an item is done, `completeAndReschedule` returns `next: null` (`src/todo.js:137`). The user sees "recurrence for N: daily" and no next occurrence is ever created.
   - Fix: `if (item.done) fail(...)` when setting a recurrence. `none` can stay allowed.

3. **A late completion produces a next occurrence that is already overdue.** `src/todo.js:138`
   - `nextDue` advances from the old due date, not from the completion time.
   - Repro: a daily item due `2020-01-01`, completed today. `next.due` is `2020-01-02`, so it is overdue and shows as done-then-overdue for years of catch-up.
   - Whether to fix this is a design choice. One option is to loop `nextDue` until the result is after now, keeping the `repeatDay` anchor. Another is to document the current behaviour.

4. **`add --priority` and `add --due` with no value are silently ignored.** `bin/todo.js:190-191`
   - `args[++i]` is `undefined`. `add x --priority` becomes priority "normal" and `add x --due` becomes no due date, with no error.
   - Repro: `add "pay rent" --due` succeeds with no due date.
   - Fix: `fail("--due requires a value")` and the same for `--priority`.

5. **Every finished recurring item keeps its `repeat` and `repeatDay`.** `src/todo.js:136`, `bin/todo.js:167`
   - `printItems` shows `(daily)` on completed items.
   - Because of bug 2, `recur <done-id> ...` leaves the item looking recurring when it isn't. Consider removing `repeat` from the completed item, or hiding it in `printItems` when the item is done.

## Minor problems

- **Numeric ids are not validated.** `bin/todo.js:198,216,226`
  - `done`, `tag` and `untag` call `Number(args[0])`. Arguments such as `""`, `1.5` or `abc` become 0, 1.5 or NaN, and the user gets "item NaN not found".
  - `done` with no id and `recur` with no id also fall into this path.
  - Fix: validate with `Number.isInteger` and give a usage error.
- **`untag` writes an empty `tags: []` onto items that never had tags.** `src/todo.js:53`
  - This only affects the export output, but it is a stray field. Only assign when the item already has tags.
- **`untag` succeeds silently for a tag the item doesn't have.** It prints "untagged" either way. Only worth changing if you want feedback.
- **`search` uses substring matching.** `src/todo.js:68`
  - `search work` matches the tag `homework`, and `search a` matches almost everything. That may be intended, but it is worth confirming.
- **Argument parsing conflicts.** `bin/todo.js:189-192,204`
  - `list --tag` uses `indexOf`, so a tag value that starts with `--` is accepted.
  - In `add`, a title that contains the literal `--due` cannot be written.
  - There is no `--` terminator, and `export --csv --json` silently prefers JSON.
- **CSV formula injection.** `bin/todo.js:172-176`
  - Titles that start with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` are not neutralized, so a title like `=cmd|...` would run as a formula in Excel.
  - Prefix such fields with `'` if the CSV will be opened in a spreadsheet.
  - The quote, comma and newline escaping itself is correct. The regex `/[",\r\n]/` and the `""` doubling are fine, and tags are joined with `;`.
- **Local-time due strings are stored in UTC.** `src/todo.js:6-11`, `bin/todo.js:165`
  - A due date like `2026-05-05T23:30:00-05:00` is stored as `2026-05-06T04:30Z`. `printItems` uses `slice(0,10)`, so it shows the UTC date, which is one day later than the user's local date.
  - The same UTC date is used for `repeatDay` (`src/todo.js:126`, `bin/todo.js:234`), so a monthly item due at a local late-evening time can anchor to the wrong day of the month.
  - Date-only input such as `2026-01-31` is safe because it parses as UTC. Local-time strings are not.

## Checked and found correct

- **`nextDue` month-end handling.** Setting the day to 1 before advancing the month, then clamping to the last day and using `repeatDay` as the anchor, handles Jan 31 to Feb 28/29 to Mar 31 and Dec to Jan rollover. I found no month-end bug.
- **Save and load.** `TodoList.load` spreads `...i`, so `tags`, `repeat` and `repeatDay` survive a round trip. Old files without those fields still load.
- **Prototype methods.** Attaching `addRecurring` and `completeAndReschedule` after the class works. `priority: undefined` falls through to the default in `add`.
- **Double completion.** Completing an already-done recurring item does not create a duplicate.

The existing tests cover none of bugs 1 to 4, so each could get a regression test in `test/recurring.test.js` or `test/cli.test.js`.
